subject: Unexpected duplicate token charges during regional failover (mid-cycle)

Cc: AtomHealth Finance <finance@atomhealth.com>

Subject: Unexpected duplicate token charges during EU failover - invoice 20261001

Hi Marcus,

We've just reviewed our October invoice (attached: invoice_20261001.pdf) and see a sharp mid-cycle overage on Oct 1st that doesn't match our telemetry. The spike aligns with a regional failover window at ~02:30 UTC when our app routed traffic to eu-west -> us-west. We suspect retries/fallbacks resulted in duplicate requests being billed.

Can you help clarify:
- Why we were billed for ~1.2M extra tokens during that 15-minute window
- Whether those tokens are duplicated (same calls counted twice) or represent legitimately retried work
- Proposed remediation and timeline for any credit/adjustment

We're on a committed Dedicated plan (DEAL-8342) and this unexpected charge will affect our month close. Also flagging VAT treatment — if a credit is issued, will that be net of EU VAT?

Thanks,
Lena Hoffmann
Head of Finance, AtomHealth

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai, Lena Hoffmann <lena.h@atomhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T08:24:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected duplicate token charges during EU failover - invoice 20261001

Hi all — quick summary from metering side after initial log review (attached: metering_snippet.csv).

What we found:
1) During the failover window (2026-10-01T02:28:10Z -> 2026-10-01T02:44:55Z) AtomHealth’s requests were routed from eu-west to us-west. There was an in-flight region failover combined with client retries.
2) Our deduplication relies on a stable request id header (X-Request-Id). In this case many retries were generated without the original X-Request-Id (the client-side retry library dropped the header on re-POST). Because the id changed, the runtime accepted both attempts as separate usage and charged both.
3) Rough token math from sampled logs: 1,184 unique request IDs processed + 1,080 matching retry patterns where payloads look identical = ~1.18M tokens duplicated (samples extrapolated). See metering_snippet.csv for sampled rows and token_count estimates.

Root cause (short): combination of region failover + client retry behavior that stripped the dedupe header. On our side, we still count requests when dedupe metadata is absent — we don’t retroactively merge those events.

Next steps I recommend:
- Provisionally mark the duplicated portion for credit (pending full export verification).
- Engineering follow-up: add a short-term heuristic to detect identical payloads within a short window during failover and flag them for manual review; longer-term, expose a stricter recommended header and doc for region-pin/resume handling.

I’ll run the full export overnight and provide precise duplicated-token totals tomorrow.

Ben
Senior SRE, Metering Team
Attachments: metering_snippet.csv

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Hi Lena — thanks for flagging and thanks Ben for the analysis.

Billing proposal (provisional):
- Based on Ben's sample, we estimate 1,180,000 duplicated tokens. At your committed rate (DEAL-8342) that equates to a provisional credit of EUR 2,360.00 (sample calculation attached: provisional_credit_calc.xlsx).
- We'll issue a provisional credit against your Oct invoice immediately upon your verbal approval; final reconciliation will occur after we complete the full export (expected by 2026-10-09).
- VAT handling: credits to EU-registered business customers are typically issued net of VAT if you provide a valid VAT ID. If AtomHealth files VAT in DE (Germany), we can apply the reverse charge for the credit. Please confirm your VAT ID so we can reflect it on the credit note.

Operational asks:
1) Can you confirm you accept the provisional credit now so we can pause collections on the disputed line? Reply with a short OK and VAT ID if available.
2) We will prepare a DocuSign credit agreement (link below) for formal sign-off after full verification.

DocuSign (provisional): https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc123-fallback-credit

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Subject: Re: Unexpected duplicate token charges during EU failover - invoice 20261001

Hi Lena — quick answers: 
1) Invoice treatment: the credit will appear as a separate line item labelled "Provisional credit — duplicated tokens (regional failover)". The credit will reduce the total due and will be visible in your billing portal within 24 hours. It will not count against your committed usage thresholds (we will exclude credited tokens from commit calculations).
2) VAT: with the VAT ID you provided (DE123456789) we'll issue the credit net of VAT and include the reverse-charge notation on the credit note.
3) Engineering mitigation (short): recommend preserving a stable X-Request-Id on retries (client-side retry lib should copy headers on retry), or switch to idempotency-key header that persists across retries. We'll share a short best-practices doc and a sample snippet for the retry lib.

I'll mark the disputed invoice line as provisional hold; please expect the credit line to appear by tomorrow. Let us know if you need anything else.

Connor O'Brien
Payment Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
